title: Four Numbers That Hit a Target
statement:
You get an integer array nums and an integer target. Return every distinct group of four values [a, b, c, d] taken from four different positions of nums with a + b + c + d = target.

Two groups are the same if they hold the same values, whatever positions they came from. Return the groups in any order, with the values inside a group in any order.

examples.why: All six values sum to 3, so each answer leaves out a pair summing to 1: (-2, 3), (-1, 2) or (0, 1).
Five ways to pick four positions, but they all give the same values. Report the group once.
The real sum is 4 000 000 000. In a language with 32-bit integers that sum wraps around to exactly this target, so use a wide type for sums.

hints: You may already know how to find pairs or triples with a given sum in a sorted array. Can you reduce four numbers to a pair?
Sort, then fix the first two values with two loops. The last two come from a two-pointer scan over the rest of the array.
Duplicates: at each of the four levels, skip a value equal to the one you just used at that level. That gives each group exactly once without a set.

explain.intuition:
After sorting, finding two values with a given sum is a two-pointer scan: start at both ends, move the left pointer up if the sum is too small, the right one down if it is too big. Four values are just two fixed values plus that scan. Two nested loops choose a and b, and the scan finds every c, d to the right of b with c + d = target − a − b.

Sorting also solves the duplicate problem. Equal values sit next to each other, so at every level you skip a value if it equals the previous one at that same level. Each distinct group is then produced exactly once, in sorted order.
steps: Loop i over the array; skip i when nums[i] equals nums[i − 1].
Inside, loop j from i + 1; skip when j > i + 1 and nums[j] equals nums[j − 1].
Run two pointers lo = j + 1, hi = n − 1. On a match, record the group, then move lo past equal values and hi past equal values. Otherwise move the pointer that brings the sum closer.
pitfalls: Skipping duplicates with nums[j] === nums[j − 1] even when j = i + 1. That wrongly drops groups like [3, 3, 3, 3], where the second value equals the first.
Moving only one pointer after a match without skipping its duplicates, which records the same group again.
Summing four values near 10⁹ in a 32-bit type. Example 3 is built to catch it.

complexity.space: O(1) besides the output and sorting

solutions.title: Every four positions, deduped
solutions.idea: Try all index quadruples, sort each matching group and keep it in a set.

solutions.title: Sort, two loops, two pointers
solutions.idea: Fix the first two values, find the last two with a two-pointer scan, and skip equal values at every level.

followups: Generalise to k numbers. What does the recursion look like, and what is its cost?
Only count the index quadruples (not distinct value groups) that hit the target. Can a hash map of pair sums get you to O(n²)?
